subject: SIG / SOC 2: admin activity logs — retention & on-demand export options
messages:
From: Matt Heath <matt.heath@mathewshealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: SIG questionnaire: admin activity logging and retention

Hi Rishi,

As part of our SIG review we need a clear statement of what admin activity is logged, how long you retain the records, and the formats available for on-demand exports. We try to avoid follow-ups, so a short summary plus any sample manifests or schemas would be great.

Specific asks from our side:
- Which admin events are captured (user creation, role changes, console logins, API key activity, etc.)
- Retention windows by default and options for extended retention
- Export mechanisms and SLA for an on-demand export (signed manifest, integrity checks)

Can you point us to a sample export manifest and confirm timelines?

Thanks,
Matt Heath
Head of Security, Mathews Health

[Attachment: SIG_questionnaire_v2.docx (DOCX, 120KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Matt Heath <matt.heath@mathewshealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: admin activity logging and retention

Hi Matt,

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise answer below and attached a small sample schema that mirrors the on-demand CSV/Parquet exports we hand off. Kimberly and Vanessa are looped in for the export procedure and handoff SLA.

Summary (short):
- Events captured: console sign-in attempts, successful admin API calls, role and group changes, user provisioning/deprovisioning, key creation/deletion, privilege elevation events, and operator actions (sudo, impersonation).
- Default retention: 90 days of full admin activity at token-level detail.
- Extended retention: configurable to 1 year or custom retention windows via Dedicated/Private plans and archive exports.
- Export formats: CSV, Parquet, NDJSON. Exports include signed manifests, SHA256 checksums, and an index file for timebox ranges.
- Delivery options: SFTP push, customer S3 bucket with pre-signed URLs, or encrypted HTTP transfer (mutual TLS).
- SLA: standard on-demand export turnaround is 5 business days for up to 30 days of data; expedited 48-hour options available under enterprise handoff terms.

I attached a small sample manifest and schema. Let us know the time window you need and whether Mathews requires a signed custody chain for import into your SIEM.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: schema_sample_admin_activity.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Matt Heath <matt.heath@mathewshealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: admin activity logging and retention

Hi Matt,

Putting in some tech detail to complement Rishi's summary so your ops/legal teams can map to ingestion workflows. Apologies for the long list but wanted to be explicit.

What we log (examples, not exhaustive):
- auth.signin.success, auth.signin.failure (user email, source IP, device fingerprint)
- api.key.create, api.key.delete (key id, actor, timestamp)
- iam.role.create, iam.role.update, iam.role.delete (role id, change delta)
- privilege.elevation, session.impersonation (actor, target, ttl)
- admin.console.action (path, params, result)

Export and packaging options:
- Packaging formats: CSV (row-per-event), Parquet (columnar), NDJSON (streaming-friendly). Index file with timebox ranges provided.
- Integrity: Signed manifest JSON with file-level SHA256 checksums and an HMAC over the manifest. We can optionally notarize via an external timestamping service.
- Delivery endpoints: SFTP (scp), push to customer AWS S3 (bucket with customer-provided role), or mTLS HTTPS POST to a customer endpoint.
- Size notes: 30 days of admin logs for a mid-sized tenant typically 1-3 GB compressed depending on event verbosity.
- Sampling: For very large windows we provide both full exports and sampled parity bundles; sampling rules are documented in the manifest.

Retention and legal hold:
- Default 90 days for hosted tenants.
- If Mathews requests a longer retention window, we can provision a 365-day archival tier or provide periodic exports for custody. For legal holds we retain matching slices until release, subject to a signed preservation order.

Turnaround & SLAs:
- Standard request intake and validation: 1 business day.
- Export preparation: up to 4 business days for <= 90-day windows.
- Large snapshots and notarized manifests: 5-7 business days.

Attached is the sample schema CSV and a short checklist we use for handoffs.

Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: admin_export_checklist.txt (TXT, 4KB)]
[Attachment: schema_sample_admin_activity.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

P.S. See SIG ticket SIG-3421 for prior export examples: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SIG-3421

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: admin activity logging and retention

Rishi / Kimberly,

Appreciate the quick and thorough responses. A couple of follow-ups before we close the SIG item:

1) We need confirmation that the exported manifest includes file creation timestamps and SHA256, and that Redwood will provide an HMAC key rotation record when delivering exports to our S3 bucket.
2) Can you confirm the expedited 48-hour export option costs and whether that includes notarization?
3) For legal hold, we will supply a preservation order; please confirm the logistics for retaining slices beyond standard retention and whether any additional fees apply.

If possible, can you send a short handoff plan we can sign (covers custody acceptance, checksums, RDC contact)? I can return it signed by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Matt
Head of Security, Mathews Health
